name: SCOC
title: A sediment model of oxygen consumption

origin.description: One-state sediment organic carbon model with deposition forcing. The compiled derivative lives in the deSolve DLL.

arguments.name: times
arguments.text: Output times; the first value is the initial time.

arguments.name: y
arguments.text: Initial carbon; when NULL, mean daily deposition over seq(1, 365) divided by k.

arguments.name: parms
arguments.text: Single parameter k, the decay rate.

arguments.name: Flux
arguments.text: Two-column matrix of deposition times and rates.

origin.details: Integrates with vode and linear forcing interpolation by default. Global outputs Mineralisation and Depo come from the compiled scocder routine.
origin.value: A matrix of class deSolve with columns time, C, Mineralisation, and Depo.
origin.example:
Flux <- matrix(ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE, data = c(...))
parms <- c(k = 0.01)
out <- SCOC(1:365, parms = parms, Flux = Flux)
print(out)

translation.description: Same sediment carbon model; derivatives are in the scoc Rust crate from ex_SCOC.c. Integration uses SciPy LSODA with deSolve-compatible forcing interpolation.

arguments.name: times
arguments.text: Output times; the first value is the initial time.

arguments.name: y
arguments.text: Initial carbon; when None, mean daily deposition over 1:365 divided by k.

arguments.name: parms
arguments.text: Single parameter k, the decay rate.

translation.details: Integrates with SciPy LSODA (rtol and atol default 1e-6). fcontrol selects linear or constant forcing like deSolve checkforcings.
translation.value: A deSolve matrix with columns time, C, Mineralisation, and Depo.
translation.example:
from deSolve.SCOC import SCOC
out = SCOC(list(range(1, 366)), parms={'k': 0.01}, Flux=Flux)
print(out)
